pages.text: $(bold)Ten Shadows$(): ten shikigami, all under my hand. $(br2)Press the $(bold)technique release key$() to open the $(bold)shikigami selection screen$(); click one to summon it. $(li)Cursed Energy is deducted only at summoning (nothing is consumed to maintain), cost = base × rate$(li)clicking the same shikigami again $(bold)recalls$() it, refunding half the Cursed Energy$(li)a shikigami's size, speed, and base stats scale with $(bold)Cursed Energy Affinity and Cursed Energy Output$()$(li)only the $(bold)Divine Dog$() is usable at first

$(bold)Subjugation Ritual$(): the other nine shikigami must be subjugated first. Summoning an unsubjugated shikigami for the first time makes it $(bold)attack both you and the target it locks onto$(); it vanishes by itself once its master or the target dies (or leaves combat). $(br2)$(bold)Defeat it to complete the subjugation$(), and afterwards it can be summoned normally to fight for you. $(br2)Shikigami roster: Divine Dog (a black-and-white pair), Nue (phantom-wing flight with lightning; rideable), Eroding Silverfish (bites and entangles), Toad (frog-tongue binding), Boar (charges headlong like a pig), Darting Rabbit (rabbit horde disruption), Healing Goat (a goat that heals its master), Piercing Ox (a cow charging in a straight line — stronger the farther it travels), Furious Ram (an orange-fleeced sheep delivering heavy strikes), Mahoraga (an Iron Golem with adaptive regeneration and a wheel above its head). $(br2)$(bold)Riding the Nue$(): right-click the Nue with an empty hand to mount; $(bold)Space$() to ascend; $(bold)W/A/S/D$() to fly / strafe relative to your view; $(bold)Shift$() to dismount.
